macro.regime: Election-clarity relief rally vs. sticky-inflation hike risk
macro.narrative: Wednesday Nov 4 had a clean catalyst: Democrats swept both the House and Senate in the Nov 3 midterms, and markets priced the resulting divided government as a check on fiscal/tariff overreach, collapsing the VIX -20.3% to 16.61 and sending the Dow +3.03% (its best post-midterm-election day since 1982), the S&P +1.58% and the Russell 2000 +1.58%. The same outcome was read as accelerating pressure to end the Iran war, crushing Brent -8.66% and WTI -8.38% even though the Nov 4 EIA report showed a surprise crude draw; Treasury Secretary Bessent's Nov 4 comment that "the world can live without Iranian oil" reinforced the bearish repricing. Gold (+3.34% to 4072.20) and silver (+5.52% to 52.33) rallied in parallel on a weaker dollar (DXY -0.58% to 101.27), a modest 10Y yield dip (~4.92%, -5bp), and fiscal-restraint/debasement hedging, corroborated by a reported single-day ~211-tonne gold-ETF inflow and broad miner strength (NEM +9.9%, HL +13.2%). Underneath the relief rally two hawkish-skeptic threads persist: ISM Services cooled to 54.5 (vs 54.8 consensus, 54.9 prior) with sticky prices-paid, pushing CME FedWatch's December hike probability to roughly 81%; and AI-capex credit stress remains acute, with Oracle's 5-year CDS near record levels (S&P downgrade to BBB-) and Meta's CDS at a record 114.79bp, leaving tech/credit markets vulnerable to a reversal even as equities rallied.

The China truce extension to Jan 10 2027 (two months, shorter than the ~6 months many expected) is a mixed catalyst: it reduces imminent supply-shock risk but also reduces urgency for the 'China decoupling' trade that drove 2026 sector multiples
Pentagon's Chinese-magnet ban (effective shortly after the new Jan10 2027 deadline) remains a structural medium-term tailwind for the basket's Western-listed constituents
